claim: Stem says Andy Carroll's £35m move to Liverpool (31 January 2011) was "then a British-record fee". It was not: Fernando Torres moved to Chelsea for £50m on the SAME deadline day, which was the British record. Carroll's £35m was a record fee for a BRITISH PLAYER, not a British transfer record. The keyed answer (£35m) is right; the superlative in the stem is wrong.
q: In January 2011 Newcastle sold striker Andy Carroll to Liverpool for what was then a British-record fee. How much?

claim: Stem states Bruno Guimarães was "signed for a club-record fee in January 2022". The reported initial fee was around £35m (rising with add-ons to roughly £41.5m); Newcastle's club record at that moment was Joelinton at £40m (2019), and the outright record signing became Alexander Isak (~£63m) later in 2022. At the time of signing it was not a club record — reports only said it COULD rise to one.
q: Bruno Guimaraes, a midfield talisman signed for a club-record fee in January 2022, arrived from which club?

claim: Stem asks which "fellow Turin club" contests the Derby della Mole; the keyed answer is literally "Torino", the Italian name of Turin. A reader with zero football knowledge picks it straight off the city name in the stem, with the other three options (Novara, Alessandria, Pro Vercelli) named after different towns. Compounded in-batch: q_fec56e asks which city Juventus are based in, and this stem answers it.
q: The 'Derby della Mole' pits Juventus against which fellow Turin club?

claim: Stem asserts Juventus's 2006 Calciopoli relegation to Serie B was "a punishment no other Italian giant had ever endured". False: AC Milan and Lazio were both relegated to Serie B in 1980 over the Totonero match-fixing scandal (Milan were relegated again on merit in 1982), and Fiorentina/Napoli were later dissolved-and-relegated. The keyed answer (relegation to Serie B) is right; the uniqueness claim in the stem is not.
q: In the 2006 Calciopoli scandal, Juventus suffered a punishment no other Italian giant had ever endured. What was it?
o: A two-year ban from European football
A permanent points cap for five seasons

claim: Stem calls Javier Zanetti a "one-club captain". Zanetti played for Talleres (RE) and Banfield in Argentina before joining Inter in 1995 — he was never a one-club player. The distractor Beppe Bergomi IS the genuine one-club Inter captain (entire career at Inter, ~20 seasons, also a captain), so the false descriptor actively pulls a knowledgeable player toward the wrong option. The 858-appearance figure for Zanetti is correct.
q: Which one-club captain holds Inter's all-time appearance record with a staggering 858 official games over nearly two decades?

claim: Stem calls Del Piero "a one-club legend across 19 years". He played 14 Serie B games for Padova before Juventus and later played for Sydney FC, Delhi Dynamos. Distractor Giampiero Boniperti is the true one-club Juventus man (whole career at Juve), so the descriptor points away from the keyed answer. The scoring/appearance records (290 goals, 705 apps) are correctly Del Piero.
q: As of 2025, who is Juventus's all-time leading goalscorer and record appearance-maker, a one-club legend across 19 years?
